core_obligations: Construct the maps (proof lines 4472-4482): choosing a K-injective representative of K and a quasi-isomorphism to a K-injective complex of abelian groups, the author defines the three maps in question by applying the sections functors and the pushforward to that quasi-isomorphism.

Reduce to H^0 (proof lines 4483-4491): it suffices to show that the maps are isomorphisms on cohomology, and by the companion descriptions of the cohomology over an object and of the higher direct images it suffices to treat the case of H^0 of the global sections.

Construct the inverse (proof lines 4491-4541): writing the H^0 groups as colimits over quasi-isomorphisms into the structure sheaf, the author uses the cofinality of the quasi-isomorphisms from bounded above complexes of flat modules, and represents an element by such a complex together with a map to the given complex, sending it to the tensor product with the structure sheaf, which is again a quasi-isomorphism into the structure sheaf by the companion results.
Conclude (proof lines 4541-4543): the author closes by omitting the detailed verification that this construction is an inverse, a routine tail.
proof_roadmap: Define the three comparison maps through K-injective representatives.
Reduce the assertion to the case of H^0 of global sections.
Write that group as a colimit over flat resolutions and construct the inverse by tensoring with the structure sheaf.
Conclude the isomorphism in the unbounded derived category.
difficulty_reason: The lemma compares, in the unbounded setting, the cohomology of a complex of modules with that of its underlying complex of abelian sheaves, in the three forms: global sections, sections over an object, and pushforward along a morphism of ringed sites (statement lines 4452-4469). The proof defines the three maps through K-injective representatives (proof lines 4472-4482), reduces everything to the case of H^0 of the global sections by the companion descriptions of cohomology over an object and of higher direct images (proof lines 4483-4491), and then constructs the inverse explicitly by writing the group as a colimit over quasi-isomorphisms into the structure sheaf, using the cofinality of the quasi-isomorphisms from bounded above complexes of flat modules and sending an element to the tensor product with the structure sheaf (proof lines 4491-4541). The author omits only the detailed verification that the construction is an inverse, a routine tail. The claim is H2: a long but fully written-out argument with one reduction and one explicit construction.
